newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Drillsearch in Ukraine gas project.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Drillsearch in Ukraine gas project.

text.p: Drillsearch Energy NL said on Thursday it had entered an agreement with Oberon Ugol Ltd, a Ukrainian company, to fund the development and production of two large proved but undeveloped natural gas/condensate projects.

The project areas -- Chabanovsky and Zaitsevsky -- are located in the Lugansk region of south east Ukraine and development has the full backing of the Lugansk regional government, Drillsearch said. Oberon holds exclusive production licences to produce gas from these project areas, it said.
Drillsearch said that in return for funding development costs anticipated to be US$3.26 million, it would receive a 51 percent net profit interest in the projects.

Drillsearch said the Chabanovsky project had estimated reserves of 50 to 100 billion cubic feet of gas. It said the Chabanovsky No. 1 well was expected to produce about 15 million cubic feet of gas a day on the basis of recent flow tests.
It said development of the project would require completion of the existing well, possibly deepening that well and then drilling a further well on the central structure at Chabanovsky.
Over a period, development would require the drilling of a further five development wells on adjoining closures to the north and south.
Production would require the design and installation of a compression plant and installation of a five km transportation line, Drillsearch said.
"Drillsearch Energy NL group has recently developed a similar project in Canada and has the technical capacity to undertake this project," the company said.
Drillsearch said the Zaitsevsky deposit was proved and had been tested by drill stem tests and flow tests.

"It has proven reserves of approximately nine billion cubic feet," the company said. "Development of the project will require recompletion of the existing well and installation of a 12 km pipeline to an existing gas processing plant," it said.

Drillsearch said it was examining acquisition of additional reserves in that area. It said Ukraine had very strong demand for gas and the gas produced from the project areas would be used in a major petrochemical plant just south of Chabanovsky.
"We have received a written guarantee from the provincial government of the Lugansk region to purchase all gas produced," the company said.

The company said both projects would also produce significant condensate. "The Lugansk region has significant upside for location of further natural gas reserves and is a highly prospective area," Drillsearch said.

Management and office infrastructure for the project will be provided by CCI Ukraine Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of CCI Holdings Ltd of Australia. CCI is involved in coal certification and coal development in Ukraine.

In return for introducing the project and providing management facilities, CCI Ukraine Ltd will receive a nine percent net profit interest in the Chabanovsky project and an approximate 7.2 percent net profit interest in Zaitsevsky.
